Elaine / team — quick technical sizing notes from my side:
- Assumptions: model variant similar to Llama-sized 33B (mixed quant) and chat-style decoding (top-k sampling) with average 140 output tokens.
- Effective throughput per H100 (with Redwood optimizations, KV caching, and batching tuned to your burst profile): ~1,400 output tokens/sec for chat flows; effective concurrent sessions per GPU ~10–12 at your avg token lengths when hitting p95 latencies in the 450–600ms range.

Sizing math (conservative):
- Peak token rate estimate:
  * Per request token: 1,800 + 140 = 1,940 tokens
  * At 12 rps -> ~23,280 tokens/sec
- GPUs required (tokens/sec divided by tokens/sec per GPU): 23,280 / 1,400 ≈ 16.6 -> round to 17 GPUs.

But there are levers to reduce required committed GPUs substantially:
1) Prefix/KV caching: ~35–45% savings on repeated context tokens if you have many repeated system prompts or templates.
2) Dynamic batching windows & autoscale: Redwood can auto-batch during short spikes and route non-latency-critical traffic to lower-cost variants.
3) Model sizing: a quantized 30B variant or instruct-tuned 13B equivalent for lower-cost endpoints where output quality tolerates it could reduce GPU needs by ~40% for those paths.

Suggested committed pool structure: (mix recommendation)
- Committed base: 10 H100-equivalent GPUs (covers baseline + KV cache gains + batching).
- Reserved burst floor: 4 GPUs available as committed but with lower utilization SLAs (i.e., pre-warmed as standby).
- On-demand: ability to spin additional 8 GPUs in <3 min for exceptional events (pay-as-you-go).

Operational notes: we’ll instrument per-route traces and token-level cost to monitor when we need to shift model mix.

—Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
